newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Madness to continue for Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Madness to continue for Belgian shares.

text.p: Belgian shares have not lost any steam despite another record leap on Wednesday and are set to discover more uncharted territory, dealers said.
The Bel-20 index closed 62.04 points or 2.44 percent higher at 2,601.56, after earlier touching a record 2,606.88, with the next resistance seen at 2,850.
"In one more convulsion, we could surge to 2,850, to complete insanity," said Tim Rovencamp at Nedee. "But there's still room for this madness to last a while," another said.
Rovencamp said business continued to be fed by retail investors while professionals kept their hands off the market.
One trader noted that the Brussels market would also be supported next week by hedging by a large brokerage of a series of new products.
But the lack of investment alternatives for retail investors, in the current climate of ultra-low interest rates, would continue to lure funds to the share market, he said.
"People are looking for a way out for all this money...(and) the lower the rates, the more people are prepared for a higher P/E," he said.
The only hitch came in late trade when the Bel-20 was pushed off its intraday highs by New York.

Wall Street bumped into some profit-taking in the wake of the rally triggered by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments, indicating American interest rates would not rise soon, in his congressional testimony on Tuesday.
Wall Street advanced further after the second part of Greenspan's testimony earlier on Wednesday.

But the mood was somewhat soured when Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin warned of the risk of higher U.S. inflation and said it was a "tough call" to decide whether the central bank needed to raise interest rates further.

One dealer said that non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere was one of the clear investment opportunities in Brussels because of the positive impact of the dollar and zinc prices. He also singled out retailer GIB.
Dealers continued to argue over whether chemicals and pharmaceuticals firm UCB, the star performer in recent weeks, still contained more upward potential.
But one said it was bound to suffer increasingly from talk that Brussels bourse authorities might reduce the stock's heavy weighting -- of about 12 percent -- in the Bel-20 index.
